initial_description:
Based on the methodology section and figure caption provided, here is a detailed description of the illustrative diagram.

### 1. Overall Layout

The figure is a wide-format (landscape) diagram with a pure white background, designed for a high-quality academic publication. It presents a clear, side-by-side comparison of two distinct methodologies, arranged in a left-to-right format. A thin, light gray, dashed vertical line bisects the canvas, cleanly separating the two pipelines.

The overall flow of information within each pipeline is strictly top-to-bottom. Each pipeline consists of four main stages, represented by vertically stacked rectangular boxes. The corresponding boxes in the left and right pipelines are perfectly aligned horizontally, creating a strong visual symmetry and facilitating direct comparison between the stages of each method.

### 2. Groupings and Major Sections

The diagram is divided into two primary sections:

*   **Left Section: "Standard Correction"**: This pipeline, occupying the left half of the figure, is visually themed with a soft rose and red color palette. It is introduced by a centered title, "**Standard Correction**", in a bold, dark rose serif font.
*   **Right Section: "EC-HTE (Ours)"**: This pipeline, on the right, represents the proposed method. It is themed with a contrasting teal and green color palette. It is topped with a centered title, "**EC-HTE (Ours)**", in a bold, dark teal serif font.

### 3. Components and Connections

#### A. Left Pipeline: "Standard Correction"

This pipeline illustrates a traditional, one-size-fits-all approach.

*   **Input (Box 1):**
    *   **Shape & Style:** A rounded rectangle with a very pale rose fill, a medium rose border, and a subtle drop shadow.
    *   **Content:** The box is labeled with the primary text "**LLM Labels Ẑ**" in a bold serif font. Below this, a smaller, italicized serif subtitle reads, "error rates vary across subgroups".
    *   **Connection:** A downward-pointing arrow with a medium rose stroke connects this box to the one below.

*   **Estimation (Box 2):**
    *   **Shape & Style:** Identical styling to the input box (pale rose fill, medium rose border).
    *   **Content:** On the left side of the box, there is a small, clean icon of a single 3x3 grid, representing a unified confusion matrix. To the right of the icon, the bold text reads "**Pooled Confusion Matrix**". The subtitle below is "one C̄ for all subgroups".
    *   **Connection:** Another identical rose-colored arrow points downwards to the next stage.

*   **Correction (Box 3):**
    *   **Shape & Style:** Identical styling to the previous boxes.
    *   **Content:** The main label is "**Uniform Inversion**" in bold. To the right of this text, three small, identical, solid rose-colored squares are arranged horizontally. These squares visually represent the uniform correction being applied. The subtitle reads, "C̄⁻¹ applied identically".
    *   **Connection:** A final rose-colored arrow points downwards to the result box.

*   **Result (Box 4):**
    *   **Shape & Style:** This box signifies a negative outcome. It is a rounded rectangle with a light red fill and a thick, strong red border, giving it emphasis. It has a more pronounced shadow than the other boxes.
    *   **Content:** On the far left, a small, solid red warning triangle icon is displayed. The main text, in a bold, dark red font, reads "**Bias Amplification**". The subtitle below explains the failure mode: "over-corrects low-error, under-corrects high-error".

#### B. Right Pipeline: "EC-HTE (Ours)"

This pipeline illustrates the proposed, more nuanced approach.

*   **Input (Box 1):**
    *   **Shape & Style:** A rounded rectangle with a very pale teal fill, a medium teal border, and a subtle drop shadow.
    *   **Content:** The bold primary text is "**LLM Labels Ẑ + Expert Sample**". The italicized subtitle below reads, "stratified validation labels".
    *   **Connection:** A downward-pointing arrow with a medium teal stroke connects to the box below.

*   **Estimation (Box 2):**
    *   **Shape & Style:** Identical styling to the input box (pale teal fill, medium teal border).
    *   **Content:** On the left, there is an icon of three small 3x3 grids arranged side-by-side, symbolizing per-subgroup confusion matrices. To the right of the icon, the bold text is "**Hierarchical Bayes**". The subtitle explains, "per-subgroup Ĉₛ with partial pooling".
    *   **Connection:** An identical teal-colored arrow points downwards.

*   **Correction (Box 3):**
    *   **Shape & Style:** Identical styling to the previous boxes.
    *   **Content:** The main label is "**Stratified Inversion + κ-guard**" in bold. To the right, three solid light-teal squares of distinctly *different sizes* (small, medium, and large) are shown, visually representing the tailored correction applied to each subgroup. The subtitle is "Ĉₛ⁻¹ tailored to each subgroup".
    *   **Connection:** A final teal-colored arrow points to the result.

*   **Result (Box 4):**
    *   **Shape & Style:** This box signifies a positive outcome. It is a rounded rectangle with a light, fresh green fill and a thick, vibrant green border. It also has a more pronounced shadow.
    *   **Content:** On the far left, a simple, thick green checkmark icon is displayed. The main text, in a bold, dark teal font, reads "**Corrected CATE + CI**". The subtitle below highlights the benefits: "bias reduced, uncertainty propagated".

### 4. Styling Summary

*   **Aesthetic:** The overall style is clean, minimalist, and professional, suitable for a top-tier scientific publication. It prioritizes clarity and direct comparison.
*   **Fonts:** A serif font (e.g., DejaVu Serif) is used exclusively, with variations in weight (bold) and style (italic) to create a clear visual hierarchy.
*   **Colors:** The palette is intentionally dichotomous. The left pipeline uses a muted rose/red scheme (#FFF5F5, #D4A0A0, #C0392B) to denote the standard, problematic method. The right pipeline uses a fresh teal/green scheme (#F0FAFA, #7FB8B8, #27AE60) to denote the improved, proposed method. All colors are flat, with no gradients.
*   **Icons:** All icons (grids, squares, warning triangle, checkmark) are simple, line-based or flat-filled vector shapes, avoiding any clipart or overly complex imagery.
*   **Lines:** All lines, including box borders, arrows, and the central divider, are clean and sharp. Outcome boxes have thicker borders for emphasis.
